name: Jerubbesheth
overview: Jerubbesheth is a male biblical figure identified primarily as the father of Abimelech, as noted in 2 Samuel 11:21. There is no record of his tribal affiliation or additional personal details beyond this paternal connection. His mention in Scripture is brief and focused on this familial link.
namesAndTitles: The name Jerubbesheth means 'Shame [Baal] contends,' reflecting a Hebrew proper name that was not given by God. This meaning highlights the cultural and religious context of the time, though the name itself does not carry a direct theological significance within the biblical narrative.
familyAndRelationships: Jerubbesheth is recorded as the father of Abimelech, establishing a direct paternal relationship. Scripture does not provide further details on his family or other relationships beyond this connection.
scriptureSignificance: Jerubbesheth's significance in Scripture stems from his role as the father of Abimelech, a figure involved in notable biblical events. While Jerubbesheth himself is not the focus of narrative action, his mention helps establish the lineage and background of Abimelech, contributing to the broader historical and theological framework of the biblical account.
